newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares post 0.96 percent gain, await Chirac.
newsitem.headline: French shares post 0.96 percent gain, await Chirac.

text.p: French shares closed just below their day's high on Tuesday but with a big gain after Monday's four percent fall on a shock election gain for the left.
A softer Wall Street, depressed by stronger than expected May U.S. consumer confidence, did not derail the French advance.

Investors are awaiting a televised address from President Jacques Chirac at 1800 GMT after Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday he would not return to office even if the centre-right won the second round of the parliamentary election on Sunday.
The CAC-40 index closed up 25.6 points, or 0.96 percent, at 2,680.34. Of the CAC-40 stocks, 27 closed higher, 13 fell.
Volume was 7.35 billion francs.
The market started with a 0.72 percent fall as traders braced themselves for a second selloff with the return of British-based investors from a long holiday weekend.
But the selling was limited and the market rebounded before hitting a strong support level at 2,640.

In the afternoon, shares briefly sagged from their highs on fears U.S. investors would start selling as they too came back from a holiday. "The surprise is that U.S. investors have not sold. They are still betting on a centre-right victory on Sunday," a broker said.
Opinion is mixed on the market's prospects, with some brokers seeing the CAC-40 falling to 2,600 this week while others say much depends on how Wall Street performs and Chirac's speech.
"He has got to be careful about what he says and avoid turning the election into a vote of confidence," a broker at a British house in Paris said.

"The announcement of (Alain Juppe's) departure, that some had hoped for sooner, could help the right in the second round. We hope that Jacques Chirac states clearly tonight what he expects from his majority," another trader said.

"The departure of Alain Juppe is good news but the impact on the bourse is very limited. We are awaiting the speech by Jacques Chirac. If he remains vague, then a victory for the centre-right could be difficult," another trader said.

"It is not Juppe's resignation which will determine the result of the second round. The right has suffered a serious setback and the market remains persuaded that if the left wins, there could be a 300 point fall in the CAC," a broker said.
Traders said they wanted to see indications from Chirac that politicians close to former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur would be included in the new government.
"The appointment of a Balladur ally such as Nicolas Sarkozy or Francois Leotard as prime minister would be very well received in the market," a trader said.

Investors are waiting to see on Thursday how the National Front will instruct its supporters for constituencies in which the Front candidate has not made the runoff. Front supporters traditionally tilt to the right but party leader Jean-Marie Le Pen has recently hinted he may favour the left to hurt Chirac.
* Investment certificates in Credit Lyonnais were the biggest risers, up 7.66 percent to 229 francs. They fell sharply on Monday along with other privatisation stocks.
* Dassault Electronique, set to merge with Thomson-CSF if the government selects Alcatel's bid over Lagardere, rose 5.10 percent to 371 francs.
* Dassault Aviation was the biggest loser, falling 5.04 percent to 1,168 francs on fears a left-wing government could halt plans to privatise its merger partner Aerospatiale.
* Total was 0.37 percent higher at 540 francs. On Monday, state agency CDR said it sold 3.5 million Total shares. Total and Axa denied market talk they had bought the shares.
* Elf, up 0.17 percent at 598 francs, obtained another exploration licence from the Republic of Congo.
